newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Compaq Computer trades up.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Compaq Computer trades up.

text.p: Computer company Compaq Computer Corp traded higher in after hours trading on Wednesday, up to 98-1/4 against a close of 97-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange, dealers said.

Earlier in the day, Compaq and other computer makers saw their share prices fall, in some cases by three points or more, on rumors that fellow personal computer maker Gateway 2000 Inc would warn of an earnings shortfall on Thursday.
Gateway said on Wednesday it had no plans to preview its second quarter earnings on Thursday.
Gateway traded after hours at 61-3/4, up from 60-3/4 at the close.
"We've had some trades post-close, but nothing in the last few minutes," a dealer said.

Iomega Corp, a manufacturer of computer storage products, traded close to its closing price after hours at 20-1/4 after it declined to comment on unusual stock activity. Iomega closed at 20-1/8. PepsiCo Inc stock was quiet, despite a report by Wertheim that Pepsi's second quarter earnings per share would be cut to $0.36 from $0.38 a share.
"Nothing is going on with Pepsi," a dealer said.
The Nasdaq composite index dropped 5.24 points to 1379.67 Wednesday, also on concerns that earnings warnings by technology companies might signal a slowdown in the personal computer industry.
The New York Stock Exchange said that session one had a volume of 500, compared with Tuesday's much higher 156,000 shares. Session two volume was 10.03 million against 4.3 million the day before.
